html:
A double deck bridge over the Yangtze at Nanjing, with a railway below and a road above, opened in 1968. It was the first bridge over the lower Yangtze that China designed and built without foreign help.

Before it, trains between Beijing and Shanghai were ferried across the river in pieces. The earlier Wuhan Yangtze River Bridge of 1957 had been built with Soviet engineers, but after the Sino-Soviet split in 1960 the advisers went home. China finished the Nanjing bridge on its own, in the middle of the Cultural Revolution, and the state made it a symbol of self-reliance. Its towers carry red flags and statues of workers, peasants and soldiers.

It closed for two years of repairs from 2016 and reopened in 2018. The rail link it gave the People's Republic tied the north and south of the country together.
